title: Advancing early detection of Alzheimer's disease: from established biomarkers to future innovations.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a major form of dementia, imposes an escalating global burden on public health and social care. Pathological changes in AD occur years before clinical symptoms, defining a prolonged preclinical phase. Currently, there is no effective treatment exist for late-stage AD, making early diagnosis and intervention indispensable, in which biomarkers play a pivotal role. While cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and positron emission tomography (PET) biomarkers improved AD diagnostic accuracy, their clinical application is limited by invasiveness, high costs. Advances in ultrasensitive immunoassay technologies has rendered peripheral blood biomarkers easily accessible, cost-effective, minimally invasive, and suitable for continuous monitoring, offering noval opportunities for AD screening, diagnosis and progression tracking. Additionally, non-invasive body fluids including saliva, urine and tears are being explored as potential biomarkers. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven multimodal fusion, integrated with large-scale multimodal computing frameworks, significantly improve the accuracy of early AD diagnosis. Recent studies have identified a series of promising synaptic and neuronal biomarkers, such as neurofilament light chain (NFL), neurogranin (Ng), β-secretase 1 (BACE1) and synaptosomal-associated protein 25 (SNAP-25). Inflammatory mediators and genetic factors also contribute to AD pathological evaluation. This review systematically characterizes biomarker profiles of emerging non-invasive carriers (saliva, urine and tears). It further synthesizes cohort-derived quantitative diagnostic metrics (AUC, sensitivity, specificity) of multimodal AD biomarkers and conducts head-to-head comparison to clarify their respective strengths and translational limitations, aiming to provide evidence-based insights for optimizing early AD screening and diagnostic strategies.

title: [Atypical presentation of ocular syphilis].
abstract: We report the case of a 55-year-old man who presented with a sudden decrease in visual acuity in the left eye, revealing ocular syphilis associated with asymptomatic neurosyphilis. Ophthalmological examination showed mild anterior uveitis of the left eye associated with focal peripheral retinitis displaying a ground-glass appearance, multiple creamy-white superficial retinal precipitates, and obliterative retinal arteritis. Multimodal imaging, particularly optical coherence tomography (OCT), demonstrated full-thickness retinal involvement with retinal layer disorganization, retrohyaloid inflammatory deposits, and hyperreflective preretinal inflammatory condensations. The infectious workup revealed positive syphilis serology (TPHA and VDRL), while HIV serology was negative. An anterior chamber paracentesis excluded other infectious causes. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis confirmed asymptomatic neurosyphilis in the absence of neurological symptoms and with a normal brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan. Treatment with intravenous penicillin G (24 million units per day for 14 days), combined with corticosteroid therapy, resulted in a favorable outcome, with regression of inflammatory signs and clinical improvement. This case illustrates an unusual presentation of ocular syphilis characterized by ground-glass retinitis associated with retinal vasculitis and superficial retinal precipitates. It highlights the value of multimodal imaging, particularly OCT, in facilitating early diagnosis and emphasizes the importance of systematically investigating neurosyphilis, even in the absence of neurological manifestations.

title: Spleen stiffness to rule out high-risk varices in advanced chronic liver disease: an individual patient data meta-analysis.
abstract: Background & aims Management of esophageal varices (EV) is of critical importance in compensated advanced chronic liver disease. We conducted an individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis to (i) investigate the performance of spleen stiffness measurement (SSM)-based algorithms using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) to rule out high-risk varices (HRV); (ii) develop a new model for diagnosing any grade EV. Methods We systematically searched databases for studies reporting endoscopy and SSM-VCTE data in adult patients, collecting their IPD. The main outcome was ruling out HRV. The tested algorithms were: i) Baveno-VI criteria, liver stiffness measurement (LSM) <20 kPa and platelet count (PLT) >150x10 9 /L); ii) SSM ≤40 kPa; iii) combined Baveno-SSM criteria ≤40 kPa in patients outside Baveno VI criteria. We developed and internally validated logistic regression models to diagnose any grade EV. Results Twenty studies comprising 2257 patients were included, with a summary HRV prevalence of 25%. The Baveno VI algorithm showed 100% (95%-CI:97-100%) sensitivity and 100% (95%-CI:95-100%) NPV; the rate of spared endoscopies was 17% (95%-CI:15-18%). The combined Baveno VI-SSM criteria performed best for ruling out HRV: 97% (95%-CI:94-99%) sensitivity, 98% (95%-CI:96-99%) NPV and rate of spared endoscopies of 35% (95%-CI: 34-38%). These results were robust in all sensitivity analyses, including patients with non-viral etiology (n=637) and studies using the 100 Hz module. We developed new logistic models with excellent accuracy for the diagnosis of EV, but the ability to identify patients at low risk (<10%) of EV was limited. Conclusion This large, multicenter, international study validated spleen stiffness measurement as an accurate tool to assess high-risk esophageal varices. The combined Baveno-SSM algorithm performed best in ruling out HRV. Impact and implications Spleen stiffness has been recommended to rule out high-risk varices, but the evidence supporting its use is of low-quality. Our individual patient data meta-analysis, which included more than 2200 patients with compensated cirrhosis, showed that spleen stiffness ≤40 kPa can rule out high-risk varices with a very low rate of false negatives. Its combination with Baveno VI criteria was the most efficient triage strategy, doubling the rate of endoscopies that could be safely avoided compared to using the Baveno VI criteria alone. The findings of our study strengthen the level of evidence supporting the use of spleen stiffness as an additional screening tool for high-risk varices.

Background & aims

Management of esophageal varices (EV) is of critical importance in compensated advanced chronic liver disease. We conducted an individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis to (i) investigate the performance of spleen stiffness measurement (SSM)-based algorithms using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) to rule out high-risk varices (HRV); (ii) develop a new model for diagnosing any grade EV.

Methods

We systematically searched databases for studies reporting endoscopy and SSM-VCTE data in adult patients, collecting their IPD. The main outcome was ruling out HRV. The tested algorithms were: i) Baveno-VI criteria, liver stiffness measurement (LSM) <20 kPa and platelet count (PLT) >150x109/L); ii) SSM ≤40 kPa; iii) combined Baveno-SSM criteria ≤40 kPa in patients outside Baveno VI criteria. We developed and internally validated logistic regression models to diagnose any grade EV.

Results

Twenty studies comprising 2257 patients were included, with a summary HRV prevalence of 25%. The Baveno VI algorithm showed 100% (95%-CI:97-100%) sensitivity and 100% (95%-CI:95-100%) NPV; the rate of spared endoscopies was 17% (95%-CI:15-18%). The combined Baveno VI-SSM criteria performed best for ruling out HRV: 97% (95%-CI:94-99%) sensitivity, 98% (95%-CI:96-99%) NPV and rate of spared endoscopies of 35% (95%-CI: 34-38%). These results were robust in all sensitivity analyses, including patients with non-viral etiology (n=637) and studies using the 100 Hz module. We developed new logistic models with excellent accuracy for the diagnosis of EV, but the ability to identify patients at low risk (<10%) of EV was limited.

Conclusion

This large, multicenter, international study validated spleen stiffness measurement as an accurate tool to assess high-risk esophageal varices. The combined Baveno-SSM algorithm performed best in ruling out HRV.

Impact and implications

Spleen stiffness has been recommended to rule out high-risk varices, but the evidence supporting its use is of low-quality. Our individual patient data meta-analysis, which included more than 2200 patients with compensated cirrhosis, showed that spleen stiffness ≤40 kPa can rule out high-risk varices with a very low rate of false negatives. Its combination with Baveno VI criteria was the most efficient triage strategy, doubling the rate of endoscopies that could be safely avoided compared to using the Baveno VI criteria alone. The findings of our study strengthen the level of evidence supporting the use of spleen stiffness as an additional screening tool for high-risk varices.

title: Accuracy of Diagnostic Methods for Peripheral Trigeminal Nerve Injuries: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Post-traumatic trigeminal neuropathy following oral and maxillofacial procedures may cause persistent neurosensory disturbances and neuropathic pain, yet the diagnostic performance of the available assessment methods remains uncertain. This systematic review evaluated the accuracy of diagnostic methods used to detect peripheral trigeminal nerve injuries in the maxillary and mandibular regions after oral and maxillofacial procedures. PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane databases were searched in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. Diagnostic accuracy and observational studies evaluating clinical, neurophysiological, or imaging-based methods for peripheral trigeminal nerve injuries were included, while non-English and nonhuman studies, reports lacking relevant diagnostic performance data, studies outside the maxillary or mandibular regions, and nonoriginal research were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2. The search identified 2914 records, of which 10 studies (0.3%) were included in the final synthesis, comprising n = 520 participants and k = 514 injured or evaluated nerves. The included studies comprised 5 prospective diagnostic accuracy studies, 2 retrospective diagnostic accuracy studies, 2 case-control diagnostic accuracy studies, and one cross-sectional observational study. Clinical neurosensory testing showed 96% accuracy, 100% sensitivity, 62.5% specificity, 95% positive predictive value (PPV), and 100% negative predictive value (NPV) for lingual nerve (LN) injuries, compared with 73% accuracy, 85% sensitivity, 47% specificity, 77% PPV, and 60% NPV for inferior alveolar nerve injuries. The tongue somatosensory evoked magnetic field laterality index showed 95.7% accuracy, 92.3% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 100% PPV, and 90.9% NPV for LN injury. Clinical neurosensory testing was widely used but had variable diagnostic performance, with lower values for inferior alveolar nerve injuries. Quantitative sensory testing and neurophysiological methods provided more balanced diagnostic profiles, especially when combined. Magnetic resonance neurography demonstrated high specificity but variable sensitivity, with greater clinical value for high-fgrade injuries. The highest single-test accuracy was reported for tongue somatosensory evoked magnetic fields in LN injury. Overall, these findings support a multimodal diagnostic approach when objective confirmation, injury grading, anatomical localization, or treatment planning is required.
originalAbstract: Post-traumatic trigeminal neuropathy following oral and maxillofacial procedures may cause persistent neurosensory disturbances and neuropathic pain, yet the diagnostic performance of the available assessment methods remains uncertain. This systematic review evaluated the accuracy of diagnostic methods used to detect peripheral trigeminal nerve injuries in the maxillary and mandibular regions after oral and maxillofacial procedures. PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane databases were searched in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. Diagnostic accuracy and observational studies evaluating clinical, neurophysiological, or imaging-based methods for peripheral trigeminal nerve injuries were included, while non-English and nonhuman studies, reports lacking relevant diagnostic performance data, studies outside the maxillary or mandibular regions, and nonoriginal research were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2. The search identified 2914 records, of which 10 studies (0.3%) were included in the final synthesis, comprising n = 520 participants and k = 514 injured or evaluated nerves. The included studies comprised 5 prospective diagnostic accuracy studies, 2 retrospective diagnostic accuracy studies, 2 case-control diagnostic accuracy studies, and one cross-sectional observational study. Clinical neurosensory testing showed 96% accuracy, 100% sensitivity, 62.5% specificity, 95% positive predictive value (PPV), and 100% negative predictive value (NPV) for lingual nerve (LN) injuries, compared with 73% accuracy, 85% sensitivity, 47% specificity, 77% PPV, and 60% NPV for inferior alveolar nerve injuries. The tongue somatosensory evoked magnetic field laterality index showed 95.7% accuracy, 92.3% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 100% PPV, and 90.9% NPV for LN injury. Clinical neurosensory testing was widely used but had variable diagnostic performance, with lower values for inferior alveolar nerve injuries. Quantitative sensory testing and neurophysiological methods provided more balanced diagnostic profiles, especially when combined. Magnetic resonance neurography demonstrated high specificity but variable sensitivity, with greater clinical value for high-fgrade injuries. The highest single-test accuracy was reported for tongue somatosensory evoked magnetic fields in LN injury. Overall, these findings support a multimodal diagnostic approach when objective confirmation, injury grading, anatomical localization, or treatment planning is required.

title: Diagnostic Value of Tc-99m-HDP SPECT/CT in Temporomandibular Joint Osteoarthritis: Correlation with Clinical and Structural Findings.
abstract: Background This study evaluated the diagnostic utility of quantitative Tc-99m-hydroxydiphosphonate (HDP) bone single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) in temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ OA) by analyzing correlations among tracer uptake, clinical features, and structural imaging to detect early metabolically active disease. Methods A retrospective review included 48 patients (96 TMJs) with TMJ discomfort who underwent SPECT/CT and conventional imaging. Clinical parameters included pain duration, visual analog scale (VAS) score, joint sounds, mandibular range of motion, and occlusal findings. Radiography assessed condylar morphology and cortical erosion, and a Destructive Change Index (DCI) quantified bony changes. SPECT/CT uptake was expressed as maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax). Correlation and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed. Results SPECT/CT uptake strongly correlated with condylar cortical erosion on CT (r = 0.80) and moderately with lateral pole tenderness (r = 0.51) and pain VAS score (r = 0.40). Joint sounds and condylar morphology correlated weakly (r = 0.26 and 0.21, respectively), while other clinical factors had negligible associations. ROC analysis identified an optimal SUVmax cutoff of 3.88, yielding 91% sensitivity (95% CI: 80-97%) and 85% specificity (95% CI: 73-94%) for detecting cortical erosion. SPECT/CT revealed increased metabolic uptake in some radiographically normal joints, suggesting the possibility of early osteoarthritic change before overt structural abnormalities became apparent. Conclusion Quantitative SPECT/CT provides complementary metabolic information beyond structural imaging and may facilitate the detection of metabolically active TMJ osteoarthritis.

title: Multi-center comparison of relative stopping power estimation of an ex vivo phantom using clinical X-ray CT scanners and a proton CT prototype.
abstract: Background and purpose Accurate estimation of relative stopping power (RSP) is essential for proton therapy (PT) treatment planning. Emerging X-ray computed tomography (xCT) technologies are enabling more advanced RSP calibration strategies, but may also introduce greater variability across centers. This study aimed to assess inter-center variability in xCT calibration and RSP estimation for proton treatment planning, using a proton CT (pCT) prototype as reference. Material and methods An ex vivo phantom was transported to five European PT centers and one research center, and scanned with both single-energy and dual-energy xCT systems. Acquisitions were performed in three phantom configurations, simulating different anatomical sizes. The reconstructed xCT images were calibrated to RSP according to each center's clinical protocol and compared against the pCT-derived RSP maps. Results Voxel-by-voxel comparison between xCT-based and pCT-based RSP maps showed inter-center RSP variability of about 1% in soft tissues and up to 5% in bone, with larger differences observed for larger phantom sizes. The largest discrepancies (up to 5%) relative to pCT were observed in the same configurations. Centers implementing beam-hardening corrections generally showed closer agreement with pCT, whereas the effect of size-specific HLUTs was tissue- and anatomy-dependent. The impact of these RSP variations on water-equivalent thickness in representative clinical scenarios resulted in a 2σ inter-center variability of 1.09% and 1.39% for brain and prostate cases, respectively. Conclusions This work presents the first inter-center comparison of xCT-based RSP estimation using an ex vivo phantom and pCT measurements as reference. The observed variability highlights the relevance of a comprehensive and standardized validation of xCT calibration protocols.

title: Repeated metastasis-directed radiotherapy in patients with oligorecurrent prostate cancer: outcomes and risk stratification from a large multinational PSMA PET-guided cohort.
abstract: Background and purpose Repeated metastasis-directed radiotherapy (MDRT) is increasingly used in patients with metachronous oligometastatic prostate cancer. However, the efficacy and optimal patient selection criteria remain insufficiently defined. Material and methods Within the multinational PORTAL consortium, we evaluated outcomes of repeated MDRT in patients with prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography (PSMA-PET)-detected oligorecurrent hormone-sensitive prostate cancer undergoing ≥ 2 MDRT cycles. The primary endpoint was androgen deprivation therapy-free survival (ADT-FS), secondary endpoints included polymetastatic-free survival, next-line systemic therapy-free survival, and overall survival, all calculated from start of second MDRT. A multivariable Cox regression model was developed to predict ADT-FS, and its performance was evaluated by bootstrapped internal validation using discrimination (C-index) and calibration. Results A total of 177 patients were included. Median follow-up after second MDRT was 26.1 months. During follow-up, 86 patients initiated ADT, 59 developed polymetastatic disease, 38 received next-line systemic therapy, and 17 deaths occurred. Two-year ADT-FS was 50.2 % (95 % CI 41.4-58.3). Two-year polymetastatic-free, next-line systemic therapy-free, and overall survival were 64.4 % (95 % CI 55.4-72.0), 83.5 % (95 % CI 76.0-88.9), and 94.2 % (95 % CI 88.2-97.2), respectively. In the multivariable Cox regression model, a longer interval between first and second MDRT (HR 0.96 per month, 95 % CI 0.94-0.99; p = 0.003) and treatment of a single versus ≥ 2 new lesions (HR for ≥ 2 lesions 1.88, 95 % CI 1.22-2.90; p = 0.006) were independently associated with ADT-FS. Model discrimination was moderate (optimism-corrected C-index 0.68) with good calibration. Conclusions In this multicentre cohort of patients with PSMA PET-detected metachronous oligorecurrent prostate cancer undergoing repeated MDRT, favourable ADT-FS outcomes were observed, with approximately half of patients remaining ADT-free two years after second MDRT. Given the absence of a comparator group, these outcomes may reflect both the effects of treatment and favourable disease biology of patients who remained eligible for repeated MDRT. The interval between MDRT cycles, and the number of metastases, independently predicted ADT-FS and may support patient selection.

title: Incidentally Diagnosed Pulmonary Embolism Two Months After Living Liver Donation in a Donor With Homozygous MTHFR A1298C Mutation: A Case Report.
abstract: Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) is widely performed in countries with limited cadaveric organ donation. Although donor hepatectomy is generally safe, venous thromboembolic events such as pulmonary embolism (PE) remain rare but potentially life-threatening complications. Genetic thrombophilia, including methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) mutations, may contribute to thrombotic risk. A 39-year-old female living liver donor underwent right donor hepatectomy for LDLT. The donor had no preoperative risk factors for venous thromboembolism, and a routine thrombophilia panel, including protein C, protein S, antithrombin III, factor V Leiden, and prothrombin gene mutations, was normal. Two months after surgery, an abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan performed due to fluid collection adjacent to the remnant liver in ultrasound (USG) during routine follow-up incidentally revealed partial PE. Pulmonary CT angiography confirmed the finding, while lower extremity Doppler USG showed no evidence of deep vein thrombosis. Laboratory tests revealed elevated D-dimer and homocysteine levels. Further genetic evaluation demonstrated a homozygous MTHFR A1298C mutation. The patient was treated with low molecular weight heparin followed by oral anticoagulant therapy for 6 months, resulting in complete radiological resolution of the embolism. PE after donor hepatectomy is rare but potentially fatal. This case suggests that MTHFR A1298C mutation may represent a previously underrecognized risk factor for venous thromboembolism in living liver donors. In populations with a high prevalence of MTHFR mutations, extended thrombophilia screening and appropriate thromboprophylaxis may help reduce the risk of postoperative thromboembolic complications.
originalAbstract: Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) is widely performed in countries with limited cadaveric organ donation. Although donor hepatectomy is generally safe, venous thromboembolic events such as pulmonary embolism (PE) remain rare but potentially life-threatening complications. Genetic thrombophilia, including methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) mutations, may contribute to thrombotic risk. A 39-year-old female living liver donor underwent right donor hepatectomy for LDLT. The donor had no preoperative risk factors for venous thromboembolism, and a routine thrombophilia panel, including protein C, protein S, antithrombin III, factor V Leiden, and prothrombin gene mutations, was normal. Two months after surgery, an abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan performed due to fluid collection adjacent to the remnant liver in ultrasound (USG) during routine follow-up incidentally revealed partial PE. Pulmonary CT angiography confirmed the finding, while lower extremity Doppler USG showed no evidence of deep vein thrombosis. Laboratory tests revealed elevated D-dimer and homocysteine levels. Further genetic evaluation demonstrated a homozygous MTHFR A1298C mutation. The patient was treated with low molecular weight heparin followed by oral anticoagulant therapy for 6 months, resulting in complete radiological resolution of the embolism. PE after donor hepatectomy is rare but potentially fatal. This case suggests that MTHFR A1298C mutation may represent a previously underrecognized risk factor for venous thromboembolism in living liver donors. In populations with a high prevalence of MTHFR mutations, extended thrombophilia screening and appropriate thromboprophylaxis may help reduce the risk of postoperative thromboembolic complications.

title: Evaluation of nanofibrillated cellulose as a urethral bulking agent in female dogs with acquired urethral sphincter mechanism incompetence: a prospective clinical study.
abstract: Urethral bulking agent (UBA) implantation is a minimally invasive, effective and safe alternative treatment for refractory urethral sphincter mechanism incompetence (USMI). However, repeated implantations are frequently needed to maintain continence. Therefore, a prospective interventional clinical study with eight client-owned neutered female dogs was designed to evaluate the clinical efficacy and 12-month outcome of nanofibrillated cellulose (NFC), a novel biomaterial as a UBA. Concurrent causes of urinary incontinence were excluded with clinical and neurological assessment, blood and urine sampling, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), retrograde vaginourethrography, cystoscopy, and urodynamic testing. A continence score (CS) was assigned before and after treatment, and monthly thereafter. Furthermore, the dogs were followed with MRI, retrograde vaginouretrography, and urethroscopy at 1 and 12 months or at the time of euthanasia or recurrence. All dogs were continent (CS ≥ 8/10) at 1 month with a significant increase in mean CS (p < 0.0001, difference 5.4, 95% CI 4.1-6.6). Median duration of continence was 8 months (IQR 4 - not estimable). At 12 months, the treatment response was still significant (p = 0.0010) with (n = 4/7) or without (n = 3/7) medical intervention. The imaging and urethroscopy findings suggest that flattening of the deposits with or without mucosal ulceration may contribute to recurrence. Sporadic bacterial cystitis was diagnosed in two dogs and recurrent cystitis in one. In conclusion, NFC showed promising short-term effect and a low complication rate when used as a UBA. Urinary incontinence resolved after single NFC implantation in all dogs for a median of 8 months without adjunctive treatment.

title: Sheep pulmonary image recognition (SPIRO): An explainable deep learning framework for macroscopic assessment of ovine pulmonary lesions.
abstract: Accurate detection and classification of pulmonary diseases in sheep are critical for ensuring animal welfare, food safety, and effective disease surveillance in abattoir settings. In this study, we propose a two-stage, explainable, histopathology-informed deep learning framework for the automated classification of ovine lung lesions. The dataset comprises 1052 sheep lung images, annotated through a dual-level diagnostic process involving macroscopic inspection and histopathological confirmation, and classified as healthy, inflammatory, or neoplastic. Four convolutional neural network architectures-VGG16, VGG19, ResNet50, and EfficientNetB0-were benchmarked under identical conditions. EfficientNetB0 achieved the highest observed standalone performance and was integrated into a two-stage pipeline, in which YOLOv11 first localized lung regions and EfficientNetB0 subsequently classified the cropped images. Model interpretability was evaluated using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). The YOLOv11-EfficientNetB0 pipeline achieved an overall test accuracy of 90% and a weighted F1-score of 0.88. Neoplastic lesions were classified with the highest performance, reaching precision, recall, and F1-score values of 0.98, 0.99, and 0.99, respectively, while healthy and inflammatory lungs achieved F1-scores of 0.83 and 0.82, respectively. Grad-CAM visualizations indicated that predictions were mainly driven by diagnostically relevant pulmonary regions. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of explainable artificial intelligence for objective, scalable, and biologically grounded post-mortem assessment of sheep lungs, with potential applications in abattoir surveillance, veterinary pathology, and flock health monitoring.

title: Deep Learning-Driven Multimodal Integration of Ultrasound and CT for Identifying Central Lymph Node Metastasis in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the utility of multimodal imaging biomarkers in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), this study developed a deep learning model using ultrasound (US) and computed tomography (CT) imaging to predict central lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in PTC by integrating radiomic features of perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) at the cervical vertebra 6 (C6) level. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 477 PTC patients from two centers. Using ResNet101 with Hierarchical Attention Integration (ResHAI-101), we extracted deep learning features of the tumor area from US images. Separately, we extracted radiomic features of PVAT from CT images. Univariate and multivariate analyses were conducted based on clinical data, followed by feature selection and integration. Results Multimodal prediction model performance was quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Predictive performance was validated using an external test cohort (ETC). The Multimodal Prediction Model 3, integrating deep learning features, PVAT radiomic features and clinical features, showed superior diagnostic performance for predicting CLNM compared to the Unimodal Model, achieving AUCs of 0.915 in the internal test cohort and 0.890 in the ETC. Binary logistic regression identified gender, age, tumor size and extrathyroidal extension as independent risk factors for CLNM. Conclusion This study establishes and validates the significant impact of PVAT on CLNM in PTC, providing a non-invasive tool for pre-operative risk assessment to aid in surgical decision-making.

title: Surgery to treat autonomic dysreflexia due to cubital tunnel syndrome in cervical spinal cord injury: a case report.
abstract: Introduction Autonomic dysreflexia (AD) is a potentially fatal syndrome in people with spinal cord injury (SCI) marked by episodic hypertension with flushing, diaphoresis, and bradycardia. Common etiologies include bladder distension and bowel impaction. Compressive neuropathies lack attention as a potential precipitant of AD. This report describes an individual with cervical SCI and with recurrent AD treated with ulnar nerve decompression surgery. Case presentation A 74-year-old woman with a remote history of C6 SCI (American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale Grade B) presented to clinic with recurrent episodes of AD that had been refractory to standard treatment measures. History and clinical examination were suggestive of ulnar nerve compressive neuropathy at the elbow - cubital tunnel syndrome. The diagnosis was confirmed with electrodiagnostic studies and neuromuscular ultrasound. Treatment with surgery successfully resolved her episodes of AD. Discussion This case identifies compressive neuropathy as a treatable cause of AD in individuals with cervical SCI. When more common etiologies of AD are excluded, clinicians should consider compressive peripheral neuropathies as potential causes of AD. Surgical decompression may alleviate symptoms of AD in select cases. Further research should investigate the prevalence and optimal management of compressive neuropathy in people with SCI.

title: MD2-IN-1 restores microglial lysosomal function and attenuates amyloid pathology through TREM2-associated signaling in 5×FAD mice.
abstract: Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) is a central regulator of microglial adaptation during Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the development of small-molecule modulators associated with TREM2 signaling remains limited. Here, through a consensus pharmacophore-guided virtual screening strategy, MD2-IN-1 was identified as a candidate small molecule associated with TREM2 signaling. Biolayer interferometry and cellular thermal shift assays supported cellular target engagement related to TREM2 (K D = 13.85 μM). In Aβ-stimulated BV2 microglia, MD2-IN-1 increased SYK phosphorylation, promoted Aβ uptake, and shifted microglial responses toward a less proinflammatory phenotype. These effects were markedly attenuated following Trem2 knockdown, indicating the involvement of the TREM2-SYK signaling pathway. Mechanistically, MD2-IN-1 restored lysosomal acidification and increased the expression of the V-ATPase subunits ATP6v0c and ATP6v0a1, accompanied by increased intracellular Aβ degradation. In 5×FAD mice, chronic MD2-IN-1 administration improved cognitive performance without detectable behavioral abnormalities compared with WT animals. Multimodal PET imaging demonstrated reduced amyloid deposition and attenuated neuroinflammatory signals, which were further supported by histological analyses showing decreased plaque burden, reduced inflammatory microglial responses, and preserved neuronal integrity. In addition, MD2-IN-1 reduced P62 accumulation and restored ATP6v0c expression in vivo, whereas these effects were partially attenuated by pharmacological inhibition of TREM2. Collectively, these findings identify MD2-IN-1 as a small-molecule modulator associated with TREM2 signaling that restores microglial lysosomal degradative function and promotes Aβ clearance in AD models, providing pharmacological support for targeting adaptive microglial responses in AD.

title: Responsive accumulation of ultrasmall DNA@WO3-x nanodots for suppressing tumor progression and metastasis via single-nanodot triple-therapeutic effects.
abstract: Effective treatment for malignant tumors continues to represent an urgent unmet clinical need. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) constitutes a therapeutic challenge on account of its aggressive nature and limited response to conventional therapies. Radiotherapy serves as a cornerstone for cervical cancer treatment. Nevertheless, radioresistance frequently gives rise to therapeutic failure in cervical cancer. We developed ultrasmall, pH-responsive DNA@WO 3- x nanodots to enhance the accumulation of nanodots within tumors, thereby improving therapeutic efficacy. title: Early extracranial dissemination with prolonged survival in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma: case study and comprehensive literature review.
abstract: Background Extracranial metastasis of glioblastoma (GBM) is rare (0.4-2%) and associated with poor prognosis. For this report, "early extracranial dissemination" is defined as radiographically and histologically confirmed metastatic disease identified at or within one month of the index GBM diagnosis, distinguishing it from metastasis arising later in the disease course. Case presentation A 65-year-old woman with IDH-wildtype, MGMT-methylated GBM presented with seizures, right hemiplegia, and expressive aphasia. She underwent near-total resection followed by chemoradiotherapy with temozolomide. A suspicious right lower lobe pulmonary lesion was identified on initial staging, and biopsy-confirmed GBM involving mediastinal lymph nodes was established within one month of diagnosis. Despite pulmonary and mediastinal involvement, intracranial hemorrhage, seizures, and venous thromboembolism, she survived 25 months from diagnosis and 24 months following confirmation of metastatic disease. Discussion This case is notable for exceptionally early extracranial dissemination, pulmonary and mediastinal involvement, and prolonged post-metastatic survival. MGMT methylation and sustained temozolomide therapy may have contributed to disease control, although these observations remain hypothesis-generating. Conclusion Early extracranial dissemination may be underrecognized and warrants further investigation through risk-stratified approaches to extracranial surveillance.

title: Determination of local diagnostic reference levels for mammography in Fars Province, Iran.
abstract: The most common cancer that strikes women is breast cancer. It is diagnosed using mammography, which is considered a gold standard diagnostic tool in detecting breast cancer. Despite the use of ionizing radiation, mammography should be performed according to the ALARA principle, ensuring that radiation dose is optimized while maintaining adequate image quality for accurate diagnosis. This study sought to determine the LDRL for mammography in Fars Province, Iran, in line with the guidelines provided in ICRP Publication 135. This analytical study involved the extraction of data from the DICOM header of quality-controlled mammography devices in 62 centers in Fars Province. In total, 27,345 mammogram reports ranging from 2004 to 2025 were analyzed. Technical information about mammography was obtained through kVp, mAs, anode filter combination, and patient information, including age and compressed breast thickness. Data from the past five years and projections of CC and MLO were considered in the analysis.The study determined LDRLs for both Entrance Surface Air Kerma (Kae) and organ dose. For Kae, which does not require breast thickness correction, the LDRL was established at 5.94 mGy for the CC view and 9.49 mGy for the MLO view. The LDRLs for organ dose were further stratified by breast thickness. A comparison with national and international standards revealed that while the LDRL for the CC view was lower than the NDRLs of the UK and Ireland, it remained higher than previously reported levels in Iran. Notably, the LDRL for the MLO view was found to be higher than levels reported in other Iranian studies and international benchmarks. These findings highlight the necessity for protocol optimization, particularly for the MLO view, to align local practices with global dose reduction standards.

title: A harmonisation framework for multi-centre preclinical PET imaging across a national research infrastructure.
abstract: Objective Quantitative preclinical positron emission tomography (PET) imaging plays an important role in translational research, yet variability across scanners, sites, and analysis workflows remains a major barrier to robust multi-centre studies. In this work, we developed and evaluated a harmonisation framework across a national network of preclinical PET facilities. Approach. Six identical NEMA NU~4-2008 image quality phantoms were manufactured and distributed to six sites, where they were imaged using local acquisition and reconstruction protocols across multiple scanner platforms. Main Results. Substantial variability in contrast recovery, uniformity, and spill-over ratios was observed under site-specific conditions. Centralised automated re-analysis produced only minor reductions in variability, indicating that inter-user effects were relatively small, compared to site-specific protocol variations. In contrast, optimisation of reconstruction parameters led to a marked reduction in inter-scanner variability (an average of 60\% reduction across larger rods), particularly for voxel-wise maximum contrast recovery coefficients (CRC_max^vox), which are more sensitive to noise and reconstruction settings than the standard axial averaging NEMA CRC metric. Following harmonisation, the variability of CRC_max^vox approached and was lower that of conventional axial-averaged NEMA analysis (CRC_max^avg), with reductions ranging 7--33\% across the 1--5 mm rods, demonstrating improved quantitative consistency even at the voxel level. Significance. These findings show that scanner and site-specific protocol variations are the dominant factors for harmonisation in preclinical PET. By systematically evaluating acquisition, image reconstruction and analysis related sources of variability across a national network of heterogeneous preclinical PET systems, this work provides a practical framework for harmonisation. The proposed framework is conceptually aligned with clinical harmonisation initiatives such as EARL and provides a practical basis for the future development of harmonised performance ranges across preclinical scanners. This enables more reliable multi-centre studies and supports the use of quantitative, voxel-wise imaging biomarkers in translational research.

title: 3D SE-ResUNet for accurate dose prediction in head and neck IMRT: a structure-specific ensemble approach.
abstract: Accurate three-dimensional dose prediction is important for automated treatment planning and radiotherapy in head and neck cancer. This study investigates an ensemble-based deep learning framework for dose prediction from computed tomography images and anatomical structures, with particular emphasis on structure-specific model weighting. A dataset of 340 head and neck cancer patients from the Open Knowledge-Based Planning dataset was used for model development and evaluation. Three three-dimensional convolutional neural network architectures, including U-Net, SE-UNet, and SE-ResUNet, were trained for dose prediction. Their predictions were first combined using a global weighted ensemble. To account for differences in prediction performance across anatomical structures, a structure-specific ensemble was subsequently developed. For each structure, the relative contribution of the three models was optimized independently on the validation set using an exhaustive grid search with weight increments of 0.1. Performance was evaluated using the Dose Score and dose-volume histograms (DVHs) Score. Among the individual models, SE-ResUNet achieved the lowest DVH Score (2.067 Gy), while the global weighted ensemble achieved a Dose Score of 2.77 Gy and a DVH Score of 2.068 Gy. The proposed structure-specific ensemble substantially reduced the DVH Score to 1.75 Gy, although its overall Dose Score increased slightly to 2.81 Gy. The proposed structure-specific ensemble provides an anatomy-aware strategy for combining complementary dose predictions from heterogeneous deep learning models. While it does not improve the overall Dose Score relative to the global weighted ensemble, it substantially improves the DVH Score and provides a more structure-aware characterization of dose prediction performance. The approach may therefore be useful for deep learning-based dose prediction in head and neck intensity-modulated radiation therapy.

title: External evaluation of a deep learning-based algorithm for automated lung tumor and esophagus segmentation on CBCT.
abstract: Online adaptive radiotherapy requires fast and accurate delineation of targets and organs at risk on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). Although deep learning (DL)-based CBCT auto-segmentation methods have been proposed, their clinical generalizability remains insufficiently validated. This study aimed to externally evaluate a pretrained DL model for lung tumor and esophagus segmentation on CBCT. Originally trained using C-arm linac CBCT images, the model was directly applied to an independent cohort of 12 lung cancer patients, each with 5 CBCT images acquired at a separate institution on an O-ring linac. Rigid propagation of planning CT contours served as a minimal baseline to determine whether the model matched or outperformed conventional rigid registration for gross tumor volume (GTV) and esophagus segmentation using geometric and dosimetric measures. Compared with rigid contour propagation, the model significantly improved GTV segmentation accuracy, with mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) increasing from 0.66 to 0.76. Significant differences in GTV D98% were observed between the model-generated contours and the reference contours (50.69 vs 53.58 Gy). The model showed a statistically non-significant decrease in performance compared with previously reported results on its original testing dataset (mean DSC = 0.84), which shared the same distribution as the training dataset. For esophagus segmentation, evaluation of 26 scans from 6 patients showed that the model achieved geometric accuracy within peri-target contour rings comparable to rigid propagation, with mean DSC of 0.72 and 0.70, respectively. Similar esophagus V32Gy values were observed between the model-generated and reference contours (0.06 vs 0.06 cc). Significantly reduced accuracy was observed compared with previously reported results, with mean DSC decreasing from 0.79 to 0.72. These findings highlight that DL-based CBCT auto-segmentation may suffer performance degradation under domain shifts across patient populations, clinical workflows, and imaging systems, emphasizing the necessity of external evaluation beyond the original development environment.

title: Dosimetric comparison of the anisotropic analytical algorithm and Acuros XB for single-fraction cranial stereotactic radiosurgery with a 6 MV flattening filter-free beam.
abstract: Stereotactic radiosurgery delivers an ablative single-fraction dose to small intracranial targets, and the reported dose depends on the calculation algorithm. This exploratory case series quantified the change in reported dosimetry when plans clinically finalised with the anisotropic analytical algorithm (AAA) were recalculated with Acuros XB (AXB) in dose-to-medium mode. Seven consecutive brain metastases in six patients, treated with 6 MV flattening filter-free volumetric modulated arc therapy, were recalculated on the same CT dataset using identical arc geometry, control points, multileaf collimator sequences and monitor units, without re-optimisation or renormalisation. Dose-volume histogram parameters were compared for the planning target volume (PTV), normal brain and organs at risk, and plan quality with the RTOG prescription-isodose-to-target-volume (PITV) ratio, the Paddick conformity index (PCI) and the gradient index (GI). Paired comparisons used exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and are interpreted as exploratory. The cohort is small and no independent reference dosimetry was available, so the study establishes neither clinical superiority nor an effect on tumour control or toxicity.

title: Quantitative CT in the real-world evaluation of progressive pulmonary fibrosis; the REVISE PPF multicentre observational study.
abstract: Rationale and objective We assessed whether an FDA-cleared quantitative CT (qCT) tool (Brainomix, e-Lung) identifies progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) earlier than routine clinical diagnosis and evaluated the prognostic value of baseline and serial imaging biomarkers. Methods Multicentre retrospective study involving University of Alabama (UAB), Weill Cornell Medicine (WCM) and University of Chicago (UChicago); n = 509. HRCTs were analysed with e-Lung to derive Weighted Reticulovascular Score (WRVS, %), Total Disease Extent (TDE, %), and e-Lung Volume (mL). Prespecified progression thresholds were an absolute WRVS increase of ≥ 3 percentage points, an absolute TDE increase of ≥ 1.5 percentage points, and a relative e-Lung Volume decline of ≥ 10%, over less than 2 years. We compared the earliest qCT progression date with recorded clinical PPF diagnoses, assessed clinically stable controls, and modelled associations with future PPF and mortality using adjusted time-varying Cox models. Results Among 200 patients with PPF and serial HRCTs meeting the prespecified timing criterion, qCT identified progression earlier in 78% (UAB), 83% (WCM), and 47% (UChicago), with mean lead times of 434, 847, and 220 days, respectively. Among 187 clinically stable patients meeting the same serial-imaging criterion, progression thresholds were met in 67%, 56%, and 42%, respectively. High-risk baseline WRVS (≥15%) predicted future PPF (OR 4.09, 2.48, and 2.30) and mortality (HR 2.03 pooled UAB/WCM; 2.75 UChicago). Per 1-percentage-point increase, adjusted mortality HRs were 1.15 and 1.19 for WRVS and 1.05 and 1.04 for TDE in pooled UAB/WCM and UChicago, respectively. Threshold crossings were also associated with mortality (WRVS: HR 6.50 pooled UAB/WCM, 4.05 UChicago; TDE: 7.60 and 3.26; e-Lung Volume: 8.20 and 2.59). Conclusion qCT detects radiological progression months to years before clinical PPF diagnoses. Integrating e-Lung into ILD pathways could accelerate treatment decisions and personalize follow-up.

title: Evaluation of Costal Cartilage Calcification Using Plain Radiographic Images.
abstract: Background Costal cartilage is a vital autologous graft for structural rhinoplasty, but calcification complicates surgical planning and graft manipulation. Chest computed tomography is the conventional evaluation method but is not routinely used owing to radiation exposure and cost. Objectives To evaluate, using plain rib series radiography, the prevalence, morphological patterns, and predictors of costal cartilage calcification in patients undergoing rhinoplasty. Methods Two reviewers jointly assessed bilateral 6th-8th costal cartilages from 183 rhinoplasty patients (1,098 rib segments) on preoperative chest radiographs, grading calcification (0-4) and classifying morphological pattern (marginal, granular, or central). Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of calcification presence and severity. Results Costal cartilage calcification (grade ≥1) was present in 54.1% of segments, with significantly higher prevalence (62.9% vs 46.6%, P < 0.001) and severity in females than males. Calcification was predominantly marginal in males (95.4%), whereas 15.1% and 17.6% of females showed granular and central patterns, respectively. Severe calcification (grade ≥3) peaked unexpectedly in the 40-49-year group (25.8%) rather than in older patients. On multivariable analysis, female sex (OR 3.01; 95% CI, 1.11-8.12) and age 40-49 years (OR 6.28; 95% CI, 1.69-23.36) were independent predictors of severe calcification. Conclusions Routine rib series imaging should be considered even in younger candidates to optimize donor site selection and avoid unexpected intraoperative findings.

title: The Importance of Molecular Imaging Response Criteria: Rationale and Overview.
abstract: Assessment of therapeutic response in oncology is fundamental for evaluating treatment efficacy, guiding clinical decision-making, and determining prognosis. Historically, response evaluation relied primarily on anatomical imaging criteria derived from tumor size changes on computed tomography (CT), most notably the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) and its adaptations. However, advances in molecular imaging, particularly positron emission tomography (PET) using [18F]-2-fluoro-2-deoxyglucose ([18F]FDG) and other radiopharmaceuticals, have introduced new biomarkers capable of detecting tumor response earlier than structural changes. Molecular imaging-based criteria, including EORTC, PERCIST, immune-adapted PET frameworks, and disease-specific systems such as Lugano, RANO, ENETS SSTR-PeRForm and RECIP, provide quantitative assessment of tumor burden and may better reflect biologic response to therapy. This review discusses the rationale behind molecular imaging response criteria, outlines the principles of CT-based and PET-based evaluation systems, and highlights the clinical relevance of integrating metabolic imaging into tumor response.

title: Metabolic connectivity and memory in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy.
abstract: Memory decline after anterior mesial temporal resection in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis (MTLE-HS) remains incompletely explained by structural and clinical factors, suggesting that networks may contribute to cognitive vulnerability. We investigated whether presurgical metabolic connectivity (MC), derived from fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and reflecting metabolic network organization, is associated with memory performance and postsurgical cognitive outcome in MTLE-HS. We studied 83 patients with MTLE-HS who underwent anterior mesial temporal resection. All had interictal FDG-PET and pre- and postsurgical neuropsychological testing. MC was computed using a normative connectivity framework and examined in relation to memory performance, analysed separately for left and right TLE. The effect of resection extent on cognitive outcome was also assessed. Presurgical analyses revealed distinct lateralized patterns. In right temporal lobe epilepsy (RTLE), immediate visual memory correlated positively with MC across widespread fronto-cingulate-temporal networks, frequently including the lesional hippocampus. In left temporal lobe epilepsy (LTLE), immediate verbal memory showed only negative correlations with extratemporal MC. In RTLE, presurgical MC also correlated with postsurgical change in immediate visual memory. Predominantly negative associations involved ipsilateral hippocampal-cingulate and fronto-temporal pathways, whereas positive correlations were confined to contralateral posterior cingulate connections with frontal and temporal regions. In LTLE, no significant correlations with postsurgical memory change were identified. Extent of resection did not correlate with cognitive outcome. MC was significantly associated with memory performance in MTLE-HS, showing clear lateralized differences. In RTLE, presurgical MC was associated with postsurgical outcome: ipsilateral hippocampal-cingulate connectivity was linked to decline, whereas contralateral posterior cingulate pathways supported preservation. No such associations were found in LTLE, consistent with more constrained network reorganization within left-lateralized verbal memory systems. These effects were independent of resection extent, indicating that memory prognosis after AMTR in RTLE may depend on network-level mechanisms and that FDG-PET-derived MC could serve as a biomarker for cognitive risk assessment.

title: Impact of the Extent, Pattern, and Location of Replacement Myocardial Fibrosis on Clinical Outcomes in Aortic Regurgitation.
abstract: Aims The prognostic significance of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-detected replacement myocardial fibrosis in aortic regurgitation (AR) remains incompletely understood. This study aims to explore the association between the extent, pattern, and location of LGE and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic AR. Methods and results Between 2010 and 2024, consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe AR and no significant coronary artery stenosis who underwent contrast-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) were included. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular mortality, heart transplantation, or rehospitalization for heart failure. The association between LGE characteristics and MACE was evaluated. Overall, 363 patients (mean age 52.6 ± 14.2 years; 54 female) were included. Over a median follow-up of 56.6 months, 73 patients experienced MACE. LGE was present in 200 patients (55.1%). An LGE extent threshold of 2.6% provided robust risk stratification, yielding the highest C-index of 0.797, a likelihood ratio chi-square of 97.30, and the lowest Akaike information criterion of 681.06. Furthermore, predominant subendocardial-involved LGE was present in 13.5% of LGE-positive patients and was independently associated with MACE after adjusting for LGE extent (HR 3.028; 95% CI 1.216-7.539; P = 0.017). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that patients with both LGE extent >2.6% and predominant subendocardial-involved LGE pattern were at the highest risk of MACE. Conclusions In AR, an LGE extent > 2.6% predicts MACE better than LGE presence alone. Furthermore, non-ischemic predominant subendocardial-involved LGE is independently associated with MACE. The coexistence of both features further amplifies the risk of MACE.

title: Nerve-sparing resection of cervical vagal schwannoma with complete functional recovery: a case report.
abstract: Vagal schwannomas are rare benign neoplasms arising from the Schwann cells of the vagus nerve, representing 2%-5% of all peripheral nerve tumors and ~10% of head and neck schwannomas. They typically present as slow-growing, asymptomatic lateral neck masses and pose significant diagnostic and surgical challenges due to their proximity to critical neurovascular structures. We report a case of a 28-year-old Asian male who presented with a right-sided neck swelling. Imaging workup including ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging, and computed tomography angiography identified a well-defined mass in the right carotid space at the level of C4-C5, displacing adjacent vascular structures. The tumor was surgically excised en bloc via a lateral transverse approach with full preservation of vagal nerve function, confirmed by intraoperative nerve monitoring. Histopathology confirmed the diagnosis of vagal schwannoma. This case highlights the importance of a multidisciplinary approach, thorough preoperative imaging, and meticulous intraoperative technique in achieving complete resection with minimal morbidity.

title: Primary borderline retroperitoneal mucinous cystic neoplasm and situs inversus totalis: a case report.
abstract: Primary retroperitoneal mucinous cystic neoplasms (PRMCNs) are rare tumors classified into cystadenoma, PRMCN with borderline malignancy (PRMCN-BM), and cystadenocarcinoma. We report a 60-year-old woman with left flank abdominal pain whose MRI revealed situs inversus totalis alongside a complex cystic lesion in the left retroperitoneum measuring 4.8 × 5.2 × 4.5 cm. She underwent laparotomy with complete resection of the lesion, and histopathology confirmed a primary retroperitoneal neoplasm with borderline malignancy, with an uneventful postoperative course and no recurrence after 8 months. To date, only 35 cases of mucinous cystadenomas with borderline malignancy have been documented in the literature. Clinical presentation is variable, imaging lacks specific diagnostic criteria, and serum tumor markers have no diagnostic value. Surgical resection remains the curative therapeutic approach, and histopathology is essential for the definitive diagnosis, which continues to pose a preoperative challenge.

title: Myofibrosarcoma of the maxillary sinus with orbital floor involvement: a case report.
abstract: Myofibrosarcoma is a rare spindle-cell malignancy with myofibroblastic differentiation, and primary maxillary sinus involvement is exceptional. A 36-year-old woman presented with progressive unilateral nasal obstruction, purulent rhinorrhea, and hemifacial pain. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a destructive 44 × 45 × 57 mm right maxillary sinus mass involving the orbital floor and extending into the nasal cavity, ethmoid cells, and pterygopalatine fossa. Histology and immunohistochemistry supported the diagnosis of myofibrosarcoma. Partial maxillectomy with titanium orbital floor reconstruction was performed. Several soft-tissue margins were positive, whereas gingival and bony margins were clear. Postoperative radiotherapy delivered 66 Gy in 33 fractions. This case illustrates the diagnostic complexity of sinonasal spindle-cell tumors and the individualized role of radiotherapy when local control is threatened by anatomically constrained positive-margin disease.

title: Sporadic ampullary adenoma mimicking adenocarcinoma in the absence of genetic predisposition: a case report.
abstract: Ampullary tumors are uncommon and are frequently associated with hereditary cancer syndromes. Sporadic ampullary adenomas are infrequently reported and may mimic adenocarcinoma clinically and radiographically. We present a 71-year-old male with obstructive jaundice and imaging concerning for malignancy who was found to have a high-grade ampullary adenoma following attempted pancreaticoduodenectomy. Operative management required modification of the standard approach due to intraoperative anatomical distortions. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges in differentiating benign from malignant ampullary lesions and the implications for surgical management.

title: Lower-extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis after Plastic Surgery: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes in a Retrospective Case Series.
abstract: Background Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a significant complication in plastic surgery, particularly affecting the lower extremities. Understanding the associated characteristics can aid in developing effective prevention strategies. Methods We conducted a retrospective, quality improvement-oriented case series of 5 ultrasound-confirmed symptomatic postoperative lower-extremity DVT events after plastic surgery under general anesthesia at a single institution (January 2020-May 2024). Among 39,055 general anesthesia procedures during the study period, de-identified records were reviewed for patient and procedural characteristics, prophylaxis and mobility pathways, duplex ultrasonography confirmation, management, and short-term outcomes. No non-DVT comparator cohort was extracted; analyses were descriptive and not intended for risk-factor inference. One patient with postoperative chest/back pain and transfer for suspected pulmonary embolism without in-hospital lower-extremity DVT confirmation was excluded from the final case series. Results The 5 included cases were clinically heterogeneous and involved complex perioperative settings, including post-massive weight loss body contouring, craniofacial reconstruction with implant use, neurosurgical-related reconstruction, extensive head and neck lesion surgery, and posttraumatic facial reconstruction. All DVTs were confirmed by duplex Doppler ultrasonography, with thrombi involving the posterior tibial, peroneal, or calf muscular veins. Several cases involved prolonged procedures, reoperation for postoperative hematoma, or delayed mobilization. Postoperative anticoagulation was administered in most cases, whereas postoperative mechanical prophylaxis was not consistently documented. Conclusions In a very low-frequency setting, this series highlights potentially actionable prevention gaps-especially postoperative mechanical prophylaxis and mobility disruptions-rather than establishing causal risk factors.

Background

Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a significant complication in plastic surgery, particularly affecting the lower extremities. Understanding the associated characteristics can aid in developing effective prevention strategies.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective, quality improvement-oriented case series of 5 ultrasound-confirmed symptomatic postoperative lower-extremity DVT events after plastic surgery under general anesthesia at a single institution (January 2020-May 2024). Among 39,055 general anesthesia procedures during the study period, de-identified records were reviewed for patient and procedural characteristics, prophylaxis and mobility pathways, duplex ultrasonography confirmation, management, and short-term outcomes. No non-DVT comparator cohort was extracted; analyses were descriptive and not intended for risk-factor inference. One patient with postoperative chest/back pain and transfer for suspected pulmonary embolism without in-hospital lower-extremity DVT confirmation was excluded from the final case series.

Results

The 5 included cases were clinically heterogeneous and involved complex perioperative settings, including post-massive weight loss body contouring, craniofacial reconstruction with implant use, neurosurgical-related reconstruction, extensive head and neck lesion surgery, and posttraumatic facial reconstruction. All DVTs were confirmed by duplex Doppler ultrasonography, with thrombi involving the posterior tibial, peroneal, or calf muscular veins. Several cases involved prolonged procedures, reoperation for postoperative hematoma, or delayed mobilization. Postoperative anticoagulation was administered in most cases, whereas postoperative mechanical prophylaxis was not consistently documented.

Conclusions

In a very low-frequency setting, this series highlights potentially actionable prevention gaps-especially postoperative mechanical prophylaxis and mobility disruptions-rather than establishing causal risk factors.

title: Palatal Island Flap With Adjuvant Radiotherapy for Hard Palate Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma: 2-year Outcomes.
abstract: Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) of the minor salivary glands most commonly arises in the hard palate and exhibits perineural invasion, indolent growth, and late recurrence, often requiring multimodal therapy. Reconstruction must restore oronasal separation, speech, and deglutition; data regarding the tolerance of palatal island flaps to postoperative radiotherapy and long-term functional outcomes remain limited. A 35-year-old woman with T1N0M0 ACC of the right hard palate (American Joint Committee on Cancer, 8th edition) underwent wide local excision with partial palatal ostectomy followed by reconstruction using a contralateral palatal island flap. After complete mucosal healing, adjuvant intensity-modulated radiotherapy (66 Gy in 33 fractions) was administered. Two-year outcomes were assessed using Thai-language validated versions of the EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-HN43, FACT-H&N, and UW-QOL questionnaires. Final pathology demonstrated cribriform and tubular ACC with perineural invasion. The tumor approached the medial (0.4 mm) and lateral (1.7 mm) margins, which were close but uninvolved. Acute toxicity consisted of grade 2 donor-site oral mucositis treated with topical triamcinolone. At 2-year follow-up, surveillance with magnetic resonance imaging of the skull base, computed tomography of the chest, and bone scintigraphy demonstrated no evidence of locoregional recurrence or distant metastasis. Speech was fully intelligible on speech-language pathology assessment, the Functional Oral Intake Scale score was 7, and quality-of-life outcomes remained favorable across all instruments. This case suggested that a palatal island flap may tolerate adjuvant radiotherapy when irradiation is delivered after complete flap healing, with favorable oncological, functional, and quality-of-life outcomes at 2 years.

title: Biopsy of Secondary Angiosarcoma Arising in Native Mastectomy Skin of a Reconstructed Breast Without Prior Radiotherapy.
abstract: Secondary breast angiosarcoma usually develops after radiotherapy or in the setting of chronic lymphedema. We report a rare case of non-radiation-associated secondary cutaneous angiosarcoma arising in the native mastectomy skin overlying a reconstructed breast after immediate tissue expander placement and delayed deep inferior epigastric perforator flap reconstruction for breast cancer. The patient's clinical course, imaging, histopathological findings, and treatment were retrospectively reviewed. The clinicopathological features were compared with previously reported cases of angiosarcoma arising after breast reconstruction without radiotherapy before angiosarcoma onset. A 45-year-old woman underwent right mastectomy, axillary dissection, and immediate tissue expander placement for right breast cancer (T2N1M0, stage IIB), followed by delayed deep inferior epigastric perforator flap reconstruction 1 year later. No adjuvant radiotherapy was administered. Three years after the initial breast cancer surgery, progressive purpura and dark violaceous nodules developed in the native mastectomy skin. Skin biopsy confirmed cutaneous angiosarcoma. Histology showed atypical endothelial proliferation forming irregular vascular channels; tumor cells were positive for ETS-related gene and cluster of differentiation 34; the molecular immunology borstel-1 index was approximately 40%; and MYC proto-oncogene expression was observed in 60%-70% of tumor cells. Positron emission tomography-computed tomography showed no distant metastasis. Because the cutaneous disease was diffuse and surgical local control was judged difficult, multimodal treatment with pazopanib and radiotherapy (70 Gy) was initiated, followed by trastuzumab plus paclitaxel for local progression. No distant metastasis was present at the latest follow-up, although local control remained challenging. Persistent or progressive dermatitis-like lesions in postmastectomy breast skin should prompt early biopsy even in patients without prior radiotherapy.

title: Impact of body composition on clinical outcomes in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Abnormalities in body composition are common in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, their impact across different treatment modalities remains poorly understood. We systematically reviewed the prognostic value of body composition in patients with HCC, stratified by curative, locoregional, and systemic therapies. Methods Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science (January 2015-March 2025) for studies reporting associations between CT/MRI or bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA)-assessed body composition and outcomes in HCC. Results Ninety-two studies were included (35 curative, 10 locoregional, 39 systemic, 8 mixed). Sarcopenia prevalence ranged from 6.4% to 62.8% (median study-level prevalence 38%-50% depending on treatment stratum). Sarcopenia independently predicted worse overall survival across all strata: curative (HR 1.52-3.76), locoregional (HR 1.72-2.51), and systemic therapies (HR 1.34-2.20). Sarcopenic obesity conferred the highest risk in the curative setting (HR up to 3.15). title: Presumed Primary CD79B+ Vitreoretinal Lymphoma Mimicking an Ischemia-Like Macular Lesion.
abstract: Purpose To report a case of presumed primary vitreoretinal lymphoma (PVRL) mimicking an ischemia-like macular lesion. Methods Single-patient case report. Results A 74-year-old male patient presented with sudden vision loss up to the hand-motion level in his right eye. Fundus examination revealed a creamy, white-colored, ischemic-appearing macular area excluding the foveal region. Numerous vitreous cells and snowball-like opacities were observed. No relative afferent pupillary defect was evident, and no intraorbital mass or signs of active inflammation were revealed by contrast-enhanced cranial magnetic resonance imaging. Fluorescence angiography revealed a late-phase leopard-spot pattern of hyperfluorescence, whereas optical coherence tomography showed banded subretinal exudates with hyperreflective, vitelliform lesions within the retinal pigment epithelium. Cytological examination of the vitreous was negative for malignant cells. Using next-generation sequencing, the multigene mutation analysis revealed pathogenic CD79B, BTG2, and PIM1 mutations, supporting the diagnosis of PVRL. Twenty-two months later, in response to visual acuity (best-corrected) reduction from 0.5 LogMAR (20/63) at baseline to hand motions, intravitreal methotrexate therapy was initiated in the left eye, which decreased the vitreous cell density. The right eye has since remained stable at 0.2 LogMAR (20/32). Conclusion Presumed PVRL can mimic ischemic-appearing macular lesions and should be considered in the differential diagnosis of atypical ischemic retinal lesions. A thorough diagnostic workup should include multimodal imaging and cranial magnetic resonance imaging. When cytology is inconclusive, molecular genetic testing via NGS becomes a crucial tool, particularly when clinical suspicion remains high.

title: Retinoschisis-Associated Retinal Detachment in Choroideremia: A Surgical Conundrum.
abstract: Purpose To describe a case of retinoschisis-associated retinal detachment (RD) in a patient with genetically confirmed choroideremia and discuss implications for surveillance and surgical management. Methods A case report of a 43-year-old man with genotypically confirmed choroideremia, CHM c.242_245 deletion, who developed rhegmatogenous RD following progression of peripheral retinoschisis. Multimodal imaging, including optical coherence tomography (OCT), B-scan ultrasonography, ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM), and fundus autofluorescence (AF) were utilized for diagnosis and surgical planning. Results The patient presented with acute visual decline from 20/20 Snellen to 20/100 Snellen in the affected eye following progression of temporal retinoschisis into the fovea. OCT demonstrated schisis cavities with subretinal fluid extending to the fovea. B-scan demonstrated shallow temporal subretinal fluid involving the macula, and UBM was suggestive of multiple small anterior holes within the retinoschisis, though these were not clearly identified on examination with indirect fundoscopy. Surgical repair with a high posterior encircling scleral buckle (#277 tire) with cryopexy achieved foveal reattachment, schisis cavity collapse, and visual recovery to 20/25 Snellen. Conclusions This case represents the first documented retinoschisis-associated RD in choroideremia. Progressive degeneration of the RPE, choroid, and retinal layers may create structural instability predisposing to RD when retinoschisis progresses. This mechanism should theoretically make surgical reattachment challenging. This case highlights the need for risk stratification, close follow-up, and early surgical intervention to prevent reversible vision loss in patients with retinoschisis, RD, and choroideremia.

title: Paracentral Acute Middle Maculopathy Prompting Diagnosis of Severe Aortic Regurgitation and Ascending Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: Purpose To report a case of paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) in which persistent paracentral dysfunction prompted cardiovascular investigation and diagnosis of severe aortic regurgitation, reduced ejection fraction, and ascending aortic aneurysm. Methods Longitudinal ophthalmic assessment, multimodal retinal imaging, Humphrey SITA Central 10-2 testing, cardiovascular evaluation, surgical findings, histopathology, and targeted aortopathy genetic testing were reviewed. Results A 44-year-old man presented with intermittent right-eye visual disturbance and persistent paracentral scotoma after non-explanatory neuroimaging. Unaided visual acuity remained 20/25 (6/7.5; approximately 0.10 logMAR) in each eye, intraocular pressure was 16-19 mmHg, and anterior-segment examination was unremarkable. Multimodal imaging supported PAMM, with structural OCT inner retinal/inner nuclear layer involvement and qualitative OCT-A/fluorescein angiographic parafoveal perfusion compromise. The affected inner retinal/inner nuclear layer region decreased from 45 micrometres to 32 micrometres. Right-eye Humphrey SITA Central 10-2 mean deviation worsened from -3.67 dB on 03 March 2020 to -5.19 dB in February 2026 despite unchanged central acuity. Cardiovascular assessment revealed a 5.5-cm ascending aortic aneurysm, severe aortic regurgitation, and left-ventricular ejection fraction of 49%. The patient underwent elective Bentall procedure, with postoperative ejection-fraction improvement to 55%. No postoperative quantitative OCT-A reperfusion claim is made. Conclusion PAMM may warrant systemic cardiovascular assessment when ocular findings do not fully explain persistent paracentral dysfunction. This case supports cautious multidisciplinary evaluation while avoiding unsupported claims of causality, quantitative OCT-A perfusion deficit, or postoperative retinal reperfusion.

title: Chorioretinal Scars in Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection Following Prenatal Valacyclovir Therapy.
abstract: Background Congenital cytomegalovirus infection is the most common congenital infection. Ocular abnormalities affect approximately 14% of symptomatic children, but fewer than 1% of asymptomatic children. Prenatal valacyclovir reduces vertical transmission, but ophthalmic outcomes in exposed infants are poorly described. Methods We describe 2 neonates with congenital cytomegalovirus confirmed by amniotic fluid and urine polymerase chain reaction following first-trimester maternal primary infection. Both mothers received high-dose valacyclovir (8 g daily) from 13 weeks' gestation. Infants underwent neonatal evaluation, including dilated fundus examination and multimodal retinal imaging. Results Maternal treatment continued to 36 weeks in 1 pregnancy and was discontinued at 22 weeks in the other, after amniocentesis. Both infants had macular chorioretinal scarring. Optical coherence tomography demonstrated focal ellipsoid zone disruption in a clinically normal fellow eye in 1 infant. Cranial ultrasonography demonstrated caudothalamic and temporal lobe cysts with lenticulostriate vasculopathy in 1 infant and isolated lenticulostriate vasculopathy in the other. Physical and neurologic examinations, head circumference, full blood count, liver function and auditory brainstem responses were normal in both. Both were classified as symptomatic with central nervous system involvement on the basis of ocular findings and therefore received valganciclovir for a planned 6 months. Retinal findings were stable at 3 months. Conclusions Macular chorioretinal scarring was present in both infants despite otherwise limited clinical findings, and the extent of cranial imaging abnormality did not correspond to ocular involvement. Ophthalmologic examination determined disease classification and management. These observations do not permit conclusions regarding the effect of prenatal valacyclovir on ocular outcome.

title: Optimizing Cochlear Implant Outcomes in Cochlear Nerve Aplasia: The EMPES Protocol (Early Implantation, Modiolar Proximity, and Early Switch-On).
abstract: Objective To evaluate the efficacy of EMPES [Early implantation, Modiolar Proximity (MP), and Early Switch-on] approach in bilateral cochlear nerve (CN) aplasia. Study design Retrospective cohort study. Setting Tertiary referral center. Patients Forty-six children (86 ears) with bilateral CN aplasia underwent cochlear implantation (CI) between 2011 and 2024 at 2 tertiary centers. Intervention For electrophysiological comparison, CI was performed using CI24RE-CA electrodes without pull-back (conventional implantation) or a slim modiolar electrode with pull-back (better MP). For speech outcome comparison, the conventional approach group comprised conventional implantation cases with ≥12-month follow-up, and the EMPES approach group comprised those in the better MP group implanted before 12 months and followed for ≥12 months. Main outcome measures Mechanistic endpoint, intraoperative ECAP positivity; functional endpoint: longitudinal Categories of Auditory Performance (CAP) scores up to 48 months. Results The better MP group showed higher intraoperative ECAP positivity, which translated into better postoperative outcomes. The EMPES approach demonstrated clear superiority in auditory performance up to 12 months [CAP score 3.00 (2.00 to 4.00) vs. 1.50 (1.00 to 2.25); P=0.010], with significantly fewer poor responders (CAP<2) at 1 year, and maintained narrower variability in median CAP scores through 36 months, indicating more stable auditory progress compared with the conventional approach. No clear association was observed between MRI-based CN aplasia severity and either ECAP positivity or audiological outcomes. Conclusions The EMPES approach improves postoperative audiological outcomes during critical language periods and is recommended for bilateral CN aplasia to enhance language development and potentially reduce the need for auditory brainstem implantation.
